## Catalog Description

Network-Based Planning and Scheduling Systems. (3-0). Credit 3. Fundamental theory, mathematical modeling, and algorithms of network flow models including shortest path models maximum flow and cost minimization models; out-of-kilter algorithm; pure and generalized network specializations of the primal simplex method; introduction to multi-commodity networks. Prerequisite: ISEN 620 or 622.

## Course Learning Outcomes

Upon completion of this course, the learner will be able to:

- develop and apply network optimization theory and algorithms.

## Special Course Designation

None

## Textbook and/or Resource Materials

This material Is: Recommended

Network Flows: Theory, Algorithms, and Applications

ISBN: 0-13-617549-X

Authors: R. K. Ahuja, T. L. Magnanti, and J. B. Orlin

Publisher: Prentice Hall

## Grading Policy

- Lecture quizzes: 10% of the final grade.

- Homework assignments: 15%.

- Three exams: 25 % each.

The weighted average will be calculated using the formula

weighted average = 0.1(lecture quiz average)+0.15(homework average)+0.75(exam average).

The letter grade will be assigned based on the weighted average as follows:

A: [90,100], B: [80,90), C: [70,80), D: [60,70), F: [0,60).

## Late Work Policy

Work submitted by a student as makeup work for an excused absence is not considered late work and is exempt from the late work policy (Student Rule 7).

## Course Schedule

Week 1: Introduction to networks and graph theory basics

Weeks 2-3: Introduction to design and analysis of algorithms

Week 4: Minimum spanning tree problem

Weeks 5-6: Shortest paths

Weeks 7-8: Maximum flows

Weeks 9-10: Minimum-cost flows

Weeks 11-12: Assignments and matchings

Week 13: Maximum clique, independent sets, clique relaxations, and other NP- hard problems

Week 14-15: Additional topics (network science and other emerging research directions)
